title: Interference and coherence
statement: understand the terms interference and coherence

title: Demonstrating two-source interference
statement: show an understanding of experiments that demonstrate two-source interference using water waves in a ripple tank, sound, light and microwaves

title: Conditions for interference fringes
statement: understand the conditions required if two-source interference fringes are to be observed

title: Double-slit interference formula
statement: recall and use $\lambda = ax/D$ for double-slit interference using light

title: Diffraction grating equation
statement: recall and use $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$

title: Measuring wavelength with a grating
statement: describe the use of a diffraction grating to determine the wavelength of light (the structure and use of the spectrometer are not included)

title: Electric current as charge flow
statement: understand that an electric current is a flow of charge carriers

title: Quantisation of charge
statement: understand that the charge on charge carriers is quantised

title: Charge, current and time, Q = It
statement: recall and use $Q = It$

title: Current in terms of charge carriers
statement: use, for a current-carrying conductor, the expression $I = Anvq$, where $n$ is the number density of charge carriers

title: Defining potential difference
statement: define the potential difference across a component as the energy transferred per unit charge

title: Using V = W/Q
statement: recall and use $V = W/Q$

title: Electrical power formulas
statement: recall and use $P = VI$, $P = I^2R$ and $P = V^2/R$

title: Defining resistance
statement: define resistance

title: Using V = IR
statement: recall and use $V = IR$

title: Sketching I-V characteristics
statement: sketch the I–V characteristics of a metallic conductor at constant temperature, a semiconductor diode and a filament lamp

title: Filament lamp resistance and temperature
statement: explain that the resistance of a filament lamp increases as current increases because its temperature increases

title: Ohm's law
statement: state Ohm's law

title: Resistivity, R = ρL/A
statement: recall and use $R = \rho L/A$

title: Light-dependent resistor behaviour
statement: understand that the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) decreases as the light intensity increases

title: Thermistor resistance and temperature
statement: understand that the resistance of a thermistor decreases as the temperature increases (it will be assumed that thermistors have a negative temperature coefficient)

title: Circuit symbols
statement: recall and use the circuit symbols shown in section 6 of this syllabus

title: Drawing and interpreting circuit diagrams
statement: draw and interpret circuit diagrams containing the circuit symbols shown in section 6 of this syllabus

title: Defining electromotive force
statement: define and use the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a source as energy transferred per unit charge in driving charge around a complete circuit

title: EMF versus potential difference
statement: distinguish between e.m.f. and potential difference (p.d.) in terms of energy considerations

title: Internal resistance and terminal pd
statement: understand the effects of the internal resistance of a source of e.m.f. on the terminal potential difference

title: Kirchhoff's first law
statement: recall Kirchhoff's first law and understand that it is a consequence of conservation of charge

title: Kirchhoff's second law
statement: recall Kirchhoff's second law and understand that it is a consequence of conservation of energy

title: Deriving series resistor combination
statement: derive, using Kirchhoff's laws, a formula for the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series

title: Using series resistor combination
statement: use the formula for the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series
